docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for the Society Protocol Web3 Outpost—the censorship-resistant Schelling point and launchpad bridging humanity from Web3 / Nation States to Web4 / Synchronized States.

docs.title: 🌟 What is the Web3 Outpost?
docs.text: The Web3 Outpost is an Ethereum-based application designed to preserve community alignment, maintain censorship-resistant accounts, and record verified histories of contributions during the multi-decade transition to Society Protocol (SP).

docs.title: Core Purpose & Architecture
docs.text:
1. The Schelling Point: Serves as a resilient, decentralized gathering ground for the Society Protocol movement, core team, advisors, partner communities, and open-source contributors.

  2. Subjective Contribution (Accounts & Badges): Issues sybil-resistant Accounts and Badges (ERC-1155) that construct a subjective identity map of user credentials, zkTLS proofs, referral chains, and characteristics (determining WHO gets invited as Genesis Actors in Web4 instances).

  3. Objective Contribution (SPEC Token): The SPEC token (ERC-20) stores objective contribution value (determining HOW MUCH Energy each account receives at genesis).

  4. Genesis Launchpad for SP Instances: When the Society Protocol software MVP releases (in ~3–5 years), thousands of independent Web4 SP Instances will spawn. The Web3 Outpost and SPEC token holdings provide the legitimate starting parameters for these instances.

docs.title: Badges Overview & Permissions
docs.text: Society Protocol badges are categorized into Official Badges (issued by the SP DAO) and Community Badges (issued by partner protocols via Community Wrappers).

docs.title: 🎖️ Meritocratic DAO vs. SPEC Holders
docs.text:
A critical design principle of Society Protocol is the separation between meritocratic governance and economic contribution:

  • DAO Governors (Governor Badges): The SP DAO is a meritocracy governed by accountable core team members, strategic advisors, and partner communities holding Governor Badges. It explicitly avoids pseudonymous token-based voting to prevent sybil attacks and treasury capture.
  • SPEC Token Holders: SPEC holders participate in economic alignment, VIP channels, and community feedback polls, while qualifying for Genesis Energy distributions in Web4 instances.

docs.title: 🔐 The 4 ERC-1155 Permissions Explained
docs.text: Permissions control who can issue, destroy, move, or configure badges within the system:

docs.title: 1. 🪙 Mint Permission
docs.text:
• Definition: The authority to create new instances of a specific Badge ID and assign them to recipient addresses.
  • Official Badges: Held by the SP DAO Safe (0xdfdC...7579) or automated hooks (e.g. zkTLS verification or SPEC locking vaults).
  • Community Badges: Held by the community's admin address or custom wrapper contract.

docs.title: 2. 🔥 Burn Permission
docs.text:
• Definition: The authority to destroy existing badges from an account.
  • Official Badges: Restricted to self-burn by the holder or revocation by the Security Council Safe (0xCc4F...98AC) during operational offboarding.
  • Community Badges: Configured by the community wrapper owner.

docs.title: 3. 🔄 Transfer Permission
docs.text:
• Definition: The ability to transfer a badge between accounts.
  • Official Badges: Most official badges are Soulbound (Transfer disabled) to preserve credential integrity. VIP Badges follow SPEC lockup rules.
  • Community Badges: Configurable upon wrapper initialization.

docs.title: 4. 🛠️ Manage Permission
docs.text:
• Definition: Admin control over badge metadata URIs, royalties, and hook attachments.
  • Official Badges: Governed by the SP DAO Safe.
  • Community Badges: Managed by the community admin via CommunityRegistry (0xEa00...EB76).

docs.title: Badges & Account Histories
docs.text: Badges form the core identity primitive of the Web3 Outpost. Attached to sybil-resistant accounts, badges differentiate users over time by recording verifiable history, roles, characteristics, and contributions.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
All participants in the Society Protocol movement create an Ethereum-based account within the Web3 Outpost.

  • Long-Term Continuity: Users are encouraged to maintain a single main account that accumulates a rich, multi-year history.

  • Referral Chains: Accounts support permanent referral chains, recording relationships between participants that can later inform Genesis parameters in Web4 SP instances.

docs.title: Badges (ERC-1155)
docs.text:
Badges are non-fungible or semi-fungible tokens minted to accounts under the SocietyProtocolBadges proxy (0x2313...6763). They serve two primary roles:

  1. Functional Credentials: Unlock token-gated communication channels, DAO governance rights, or administrative moderation roles.

  2. Permanent Attributions: Create verifiable proof of event attendance, core contributions, or verified off-chain attributes (via zkTLS).

docs.title: The Linux Model: Codebase vs. Instances
docs.text: Society Protocol operates under an organizational and architectural framework similar to the Linux Foundation.

docs.title: 🐧 A Single Codebase, Many Communities
docs.text:
Civilization only needs one impeccably secure, highly modular, and credibly neutral codebase for Society Protocol to spawn an infinite number of customizable instances.

                  +-----------------------------------+
                  |   SOCIETY PROTOCOL CORE CODEBASE  |
                  |   (Secure, Modular, Neutral)      |
                  +-----------------------------------+
                                    |
          +-------------------------+-------------------------+
          |                         |                         |
          v                         v                         v
+-------------------+     +-------------------+     +-------------------+
|  SP Instance #1   |     |  SP Instance #2   |     |  SP Instance #3   |
| (Eco-Community)   |     | (Network State)   |     | (DeFi Guild)      |
| Custom Parameters |     | Custom Parameters |     | Custom Parameters |
+-------------------+     +-------------------+     +-------------------+

docs.title: The Linux Analogy
docs.text:
• The Core Codebase (Linux Kernel): Maintained by the Society Protocol organization. It provides the minimal-viable-product (MVP) state transition functions (STF), Energy state machine, account abstractions, and core Value Functions (VFs).
  • SP Instances (Linux Distributions): Independent deployments created by communities, DAOs, or nation-states (e.g. Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian equivalents). Each instance configures its own Value Functions, Constitutions, UIs, and initial Energy distributions.

docs.title: 🏛️ The Three Core Principles
docs.text:
To allow thousands of diverse communities to trust and adopt Society Protocol, the core codebase adheres strictly to three principles:

  1. Impeccable Security: Entrusting human identity and society to a state machine carries immense responsibility. The core layers undergo rigorous battle-testing and concentric audit rings.

  2. Modular Architecture: Communities configure distinct Value Functions (Parenting, Hunting, Property, Curation, Governance, Communication) without altering core security.

  3. Credible Neutrality: The stewards of the codebase remain strictly neutral. The core team does not start or rule SP instances; it builds the generic, fair infrastructure for all instances to bloom.

docs.title: Genesis Energy & Instance Airdrops
docs.text: One of the most valuable aspects of participating in the Web3 Outpost is qualifying for Genesis Energy Distributions across newly spawned Society Protocol instances over decades.

docs.title: 🔮 What is Genesis Energy?
docs.text:
In Web4 Society Protocol instances, Energy is the foundational resource unit used to measure economic output, governance weight, and systemic participation within Synchronized States.

When an SP instance launches:

  • It requires a legitimate initial distribution of Energy among its founding accounts.

  • Manually picking accounts and manually deciding Energy amounts creates severe political conflict and coordination bottlenecks.

  • The Web3 Outpost solution: Upstart instances query the Web3 Outpost to identify verified accounts (Subjective Map via Badges) and distribute initial Energy proportional to SPEC Token holdings (Objective Map).

Holding SPEC tokens and building an account history in the Web3 Outpost provides participants with the potential for continuous Genesis Energy airdrops across thousands of independent SP instances over decades.

docs.title: 💡 Why Instances Choose SPEC for Energy Distribution
docs.text:
Upstart SP instances are not forced to grant SPEC holders Energy, but incentives naturally align:

  1. Legitimacy & Sybil-Resistance: SPEC token holdings represent authentic historical skin-in-the-game.

  2. Attracting Active Participants: Granting Energy to SPEC holders attracts an experienced, highly aligned base of early adopters.

  3. Automated Scale: Using SPEC and Badges eliminates manual invite negotiations, enabling instances to launch at scale on day one.

docs.title: Web3 Outpost: The Web4 Launchpad
docs.text: The Web3 Outpost functions as the central Schelling point and launchpad bridging humanity from Web3 and Nation States into Web4 and Synchronized States.

docs.title: 🚀 The Launchpad Concept
docs.text:
Building the full Society Protocol ecosystem is a multi-decade journey. The minimal-viable-product (MVP) codebase is expected in ~3–5 years, while the overall transition of human society into Synchronized States will stretch over 20 to 75 years.

During this transition, the Web3 Outpost provides crucial censorship-resistant infrastructure on Ethereum Mainnet to:

  1. Build a Subjective Identity Map (Accounts & Badges): Users construct a single, sybil-resistant history recorded via Accounts and Badges (ERC-1155), capturing credentials, referral chains, and characteristics.

  2. Measure Objective Contribution (SPEC Token): The SPEC token (ERC-20) stores objective contribution value, quantifying participant skin-in-the-game.

  3. Supply Genesis Starting Parameters: When independent Web4 Society Protocol instances spawn, they need to know who to include (Subjective Map) and how much Energy to grant (Objective Map).

docs.title: ⚡ How the Outpost Powers Web4 Instances
docs.text:
When a community, family, DAO, or nation-state decides to launch a new Society Protocol Instance, they face two fundamental questions:

  1. "Who gets to be the initial Genesis Actors in our instance?" (Answered by Accounts & Badges)

  2. "How much initial Energy does each Genesis Actor receive?" (Answered by SPEC Token Holdings)

Attempting to resolve these questions manually for thousands of participants creates severe coordination friction, sybil vulnerability, and political deadlock.

The Web3 Outpost resolves this friction:

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                           WEB3 OUTPOST                                  |
|                                                                         |
|  [Subjective Map] Accounts + Badges (zkTLS, Builder, Country, Roles)    |
|  [Objective Map]  SPEC Token Balances (Stored Contribution Value)       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    |
                                    | Exports Genesis Parameters
                                    v
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  UPSTART WEB4 SP INSTANCES (GENESIS)                    |
|                                                                         |
|  - Community A Instance   --> Invites Builder Badges (Who) + SPEC (Energy)
|  - Community B Instance   --> Invites Argentine Badges (Who) + SPEC (Energy)
|  - Network State Instance --> Invites All Outpost Accounts + SPEC (Energy)
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: Examples of Community Genesis Parameters
docs.text:
Communities launching SP instances can slice the Web3 Outpost data in endless ways:

  • Builder-Focused Instance: Invites only accounts possessing the Builder Badge (26), allocating initial Energy proportional to each account's SPEC token holdings.
  • Regional Network State: Invites only accounts with a verified Country Badge (via zkTLS), requiring a minimum SPEC balance for sybil-resistance, and allocating equal starting Energy.
  • Partner Community Instance: Invites members holding custom Community Wrapper Badges and grants bonus Energy to SPEC token holders.

docs.title: SPEC Token: Objective Contribution & Economics
docs.text: The SPEC Token (0x6AcD7735B3acF0DD677332a599FFfF71C18818BA) is the objective contribution storage token of the Society Protocol movement. It works alongside the account system to provide a real-time, sybil-resistant community map on Ethereum.

docs.title: ⚖️ Subjective vs. Objective Contribution
docs.text:
To understand how the Web3 Outpost enables the launching of Web4 Society Protocol (SP) instances, contributions are separated into two distinct layers:

Layer System Role in Web4 Genesis Example Subjective Contribution Accounts & Badges (ERC-1155) Determines WHO gets invited as Genesis Actors "Invite accounts with Builder Badge" or "Invite verified Argentine accounts" Objective Contribution SPEC Token (ERC-20) Determines HOW MUCH Energy each account receives "Allocate Energy proportional to SPEC balance" or "Equal Energy if SPEC > X"

Together, Subjective Accounts and Objective SPEC holdings form a sybil-resistant community map. Upstart SP instances use this map to launch cohesive, legitimate instances populated by interested participants at scale.

docs.title: 🎯 Use Cases of the SPEC Token
1. Primary Use Case: Genesis Energy Allocation (~75 Year Horizon)
docs.text: The primary function of SPEC is to be held as stored contribution value. Upstart Web4 SP instances recognize SPEC token holdings to allocate initial Energy distributions to legitimate participants. The Web3 Outpost remains active and valuable for decades to facilitate this launchpad transition.

docs.title: 2. VIP Rooms (Gold, Silver, Bronze)
docs.text: Users lock SPEC tokens to enter exclusive, spam-free VIP communication channels. This allows committed participants to form long-term relationships and strategic partnerships.

docs.title: 3. Liquidity Provision (LP Rewards)
docs.text: 5% of the total SPEC supply (500,000,000 SPEC) is earmarked for liquidity providers in the SPEC/WETH pool, distributed evenly over a 5-year period.

docs.title: 4. Potential Future Outpost Features
docs.text:
• Curation Mechanics: Using SPEC for upvoting and curating forum and communication posts (implementing an infantile version of the Curation Value Function).
  • Encrypted Web3 Comms: Payment for E2EE messaging storage and Web3 social media features (infantile Farming Value Function).
  • NFT Platform Extensions: Access and discounts on custom avatar and flag collections for community differentiation.

docs.title: 🗳️ Governance Role: Parallel Feedback (Non-Voting)
docs.text:
To prevent sybil attacks and economic treasury capture (which plague traditional Web3 token-voting DAOs), SPEC is not used for direct execution voting in the SP DAO.

  • Meritocratic Governance: Execution decisions are made exclusively by Governor Badges held by accountable core team members, advisors, and partner communities.
  • Community Parallel Feedback: SPEC token holders can run parallel feedback votes on governance proposals. Governors review this feedback to gauge broader community sentiment before executing decisions.
  • Modular Decision Delegation: In the future, Governors may delegate specific modular decision-making power to SPEC holders on a per-decision basis.

docs.title: How to Create Community Badges
docs.text: This guide explains how third-party DAOs, NFT projects, and Web3 protocols can deploy custom ERC-1155 badge contracts using Society Protocol's CommunityWrapperFactory (0x84ffd2805af9d0946e02Fe19Cd1eE58228669B0e).

docs.title: 💡 Overview
docs.text:
Deploying custom badges through the factory provides your project with instant compatibility across Society Protocol's ecosystem:

  • No Smart Contract Coding: Initialize permissioned ERC-1155 badges via single factory calls.
  • Automatic Registry Indexing: Deployed wrappers register immediately in CommunityRegistry (0xEa00...EB76).
  • Custom Minting & Transfer Rules: Define whether your badges are soulbound, burnable, or transferable.

docs.title: Method 1: Web Interface (Recommended)
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the Community Developer Console.

  2. Connect your community admin wallet (or Safe multisig).

  3. Fill out your community metadata:

  4. Community Name: (e.g. Acme DAO)
  5. Badge Symbol: (e.g. ACME)

  6. Base URI: ipfs://.../ (Metadata directory URI)

  7. Select permission flags (Mintable by admin, Transferable, Burnable).

  8. Click Deploy Community Wrapper and execute the transaction.

docs.title: Method 2: Smart Contract Interaction (CLI / Foundry / Hardhat)
docs.text:
Developers can interact directly with CommunityWrapperFactory at 0x84ffd2805af9d0946e02Fe19Cd1eE58228669B0e.

// Interface Excerpt
interface ICommunityWrapperFactory {
    function createCommunityWrapper(
        string memory name,
        string memory symbol,
        string memory baseURI,
        address admin,
        bool isSoulbound
    ) external returns (address wrapperAddress);
}

docs.title: Example Deployment via Foundry Cast:
docs.text:
cast send 0x84ffd2805af9d0946e02Fe19Cd1eE58228669B0e \
  "createCommunityWrapper(string,string,string,address,bool)" \
  "Acme Community" "ACME" "ipfs://QmYourHash/" 0xYourAdminAddress true \
  --rpc-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_API_KEY \
  --private-key $PRIVATE_KEY

docs.title: ⚙️ Post-Deployment Management
docs.text:
Once deployed:

  1. Minting Badges: The assigned admin address can call mintBadge(address to, uint256 id, uint256 amount) on the returned CommunityWrapper instance.

  2. Hook Integration: Attach optional hooks (e.g. SingleMintHook or custom gating logic) to restrict issuance parameters.

docs.title: FAQ & zkTLS Verification
docs.text: This page answers Frequently Asked Questions and provides a deep dive into zkTLS & Off-Chain Verification, explaining how Web2 credentials and private data are brought on-chain to claim badges without compromising privacy.

docs.title: 🔒 What is zkTLS & Off-Chain Verification?
docs.text: zkTLS (Zero-Knowledge Transport Layer Security) is a cryptographic technology that allows users to generate zero-knowledge proofs of Web2 TLS web sessions (e.g. logging into Twitter, GitHub, bank portals, or government passport verification systems).

docs.title: Key Benefits
docs.text:
1. Privacy-Preserving: Proven credentials (e.g. "User is over 18" or "User holds verified GitHub account") are verified on-chain without revealing passwords, personal identifying information, or API tokens.

  2. Trustless Verification: Proofs are verified directly by Society Protocol smart contract hooks (such as SingleMintHook at 0xc5cA...FC6D).

  3. Sybil Resistance: Prevents bot farming by linking unique physical or off-chain identity proofs to single Ethereum addresses.

docs.title: Q: Do I need to pay gas to claim badges?
docs.text: A: Official badges minted on Ethereum Mainnet require standard gas. However, for select community badges, gasless meta-transactions (EIP-712) or Layer-2 wrapper deployments are supported.

docs.title: Q: Are official badges transferable?
docs.text: A: Most official governance and role badges (IDs 11–13, 24–28) are Soulbound (non-transferable) to protect credential integrity. VIP Badges (IDs 14–16) are tied to SPEC lockup vaults and burn upon token withdrawal.

docs.title: Q: What happens if I lose access to my wallet?
docs.text: A: Because official badges are cryptographically tied to your wallet address, you must re-verify your identity or re-lock SPEC tokens from a new wallet address. Security Council revocation can clear lost address holdings upon request.

docs.title: Q: Where is badge metadata stored?
docs.text: A: All badge metadata JSON files and visual assets are permanently pinned to IPFS and indexed by CommunityRegistry (0xEa008f15E1454C79D6AA7B95Dd3E1d39Ba32EB76).

docs.title: Q: Can I use Society Protocol badges in my Discord server?
docs.text: A: Yes! Any Discord server can integrate Guild.xyz, Collab.Land, or Society Protocol's native OAuth bot pointing to SocietyProtocolBadges (0x2313...6763).

docs.title: How to Lock SPEC to Get VIP Badges
docs.text: This step-by-step tutorial guides community members on how to lock SPEC tokens (0x6AcD...18BA) to claim Bronze, Silver, or Gold VIP Badges and unlock access to token-gated communication rooms.

docs.title: 📱 Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, ensure you have:

  1. An Ethereum Web3 Wallet (e.g. MetaMask, WalletConnect, Rabby).

  2. Sufficient ETH for Mainnet gas fees.

  3. Sufficient SPEC tokens in your wallet for your desired VIP Tier:

  4. Bronze VIP (ID: 14): 1,000 SPEC (30 days minimum lockup)
  5. Silver VIP (ID: 15): 10,000 SPEC (90 days minimum lockup)
  6. Gold VIP (ID: 16): 100,000 SPEC (180 days minimum lockup)

docs.title: Step 1: Access the Society Protocol Portal
docs.text:
Navigate to the official dApp interface: 👉 Society Protocol Portal (https://app.societyprotocol.io/vip)

[!CAUTION] Always verify the URL and ensure your browser is connected to Ethereum Mainnet before signing transactions.

docs.title: Step 2: Connect Your Wallet
docs.text:
1. Click Connect Wallet in the top right corner.

  2. Select your Web3 provider (MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, etc.).

  3. Authenticate the session signature request.

docs.title: Step 3: Approve SPEC Token Lockup
docs.text:
Smart contracts require your explicit approval before transferring SPEC tokens into the lockup vault:

  1. Select your target VIP Tier (Bronze, Silver, or Gold).

  2. Click Approve SPEC.

  3. Confirm the ERC-20 token approval transaction in your wallet UI.

docs.title: Step 4: Lock SPEC & Mint VIP Badge
docs.text:
1. Once the approval transaction is confirmed, click Lock SPEC & Claim Badge.

  2. Review the transaction parameters:

  3. Lock Duration: Selected duration (e.g. 90 days for Silver).

  4. Badge ID: Target ERC-1155 token ID (e.g. 15).

  5. Confirm the transaction in your wallet.

docs.title: Step 5: Verify Badge Receipt & Join VIP Channels
docs.text:
After transaction confirmation on Ethereum Mainnet:

  • Your wallet will instantly receive the corresponding ERC-1155 VIP Badge (SocietyProtocolBadges proxy: 0x2313...6763).
  • Connect your wallet to Discord or Telegram via our verification bot to automatically claim your VIP roles.

docs.title: 🔓 How Unlocking Works
docs.text:
• When your lockup period expires, you can visit the My Vaults section on the portal to withdraw your SPEC tokens.
  • Important: Withdrawing your locked SPEC tokens automatically burns your VIP Badge, forfeiting channel access until tokens are re-locked.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architectural Overview
docs.text:
1. ERC-1967 Proxies: Core contracts (SocietyProtocolBadges, CommunityWrapperFactory, CommunityRegistry) use transparent proxies. Integrations interact exclusively with proxy addresses.

  2. Multisig Safes: Treasury and contract upgrades are managed by the SP DAO Safe (0xdfdC...7579). Emergency circuit breakers are managed by the Security Council Safe (0xCc4F...98AC).

  3. Hooks: SingleMintHook (0xc5cA...FC6D) enforces strict single-token limits per account for soulbound badges.
